A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bregman Frank–Wolfe research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original optimization experiments on synthetic instances, gas-sensor data and MovieLens, including convergence plots and mean ± standard deviation over 20 instances in Tables 2–8.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments in Section 6 and Appendix F and adds projected-gradient results to the gas-sensor comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects the acceptance logic: v4 computes the trial step before checking sufficient decrease, returns on success, and updates M and kappa after failure. v2 tests the acceptance inequality in a while loop before defining the trial quantities. The step-size formula and FW/away-step updates are retained.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same gas-sensor, phase-retrieval, nonnegative inverse-problem, low-rank minimization and NMF coverage, including MovieLens 100K. v4's added blind-deconvolution, KL-NMF and scalar-function examples are mathematical illustrations, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: v4 adds projected gradient descent, named ProjGD, to the gas-sensor comparisons in Section 6.1 and Figures 1–2. The EucFW and OpenFW comparators there, and comparator membership in the other experiments, are retained.

E3.justification: The reported data generation, dimensions, constraints, initialization, iteration budgets, primal/FW-gap metrics and 10^-7 stopping criterion are retained. ProjGD enters the existing gas-sensor evaluation without a separately reported change to its evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The existing comparisons across constraint radii, problem sizes and FW/away-step settings are retained. No new empirical ablation, sensitivity, robustness or error analysis is added; the new appendix examples are theoretical.

E5.justification: Tables 2–8 retain mean ± standard deviation over 20 different instances, and the stated seeds remain 1234 and 42. The new reproducibility statement reiterates statistical practices without reporting additional repetitions or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 add ProjGD curves showing larger final primal and FW gaps than BregFW. Figures 3–10 and every numerical entry in Tables 2–8 are unchanged, including the mixed primal-gap/FW-gap rankings for away-step phase retrieval and NMF.

T1.justification: v4 adds the line-search evaluation bound in Theorem 3.3 and its Appendix B.3 proof, plus worked mathematical examples in B.5 and E.5. Lemma C.5 tightens v2 Lemma B.5's rho ≤ mu assumption to rho < mu. The principal convergence results are retained. New Example E.5(i) contains an incorrect stated sublevel bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: adaptive Bregman FW and away-step FW, convergence under smooth adaptability and growth assumptions, local nonconvex convergence, and empirical advantages. Additional supporting material does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Remark B.6 newly discusses the difficulty of selecting the best kernel and suggests matching the objective's elementary structure. Section 5 expands explanations of the roles of weak convexity, quadratic growth and PL conditions. The existing convergence limitations and DC-optimization future direction remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds a reproducibility statement asserting that evaluation code, configurations and scripts accompany the paper, and that preprocessing is documented. The supplied PDFs cannot verify those supplementary files. Reported Julia version, hardware and numerical hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A expands discussion of mirror descent and Bregman proximal methods, adding works including Krichene et al., Allen-Zhu and Orecchia, and Fujiki et al. Boț et al. and Stella et al. support the new restoration example. The central positioning relative to existing FW methods remains.

P1.justification: v4 polishes sentences, shortens the notation preamble, relocates supporting lemmas to appendices and removes duplicate theorem statements while retaining their proofs. Related-work and disclosure sections are added. The seven-section main narrative and most existing exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset into the ICLR layout, changing typography, title/authors, headers, spacing and display placement. Algorithms 1–2 become compact displays beside prose, and tables and figures are resized and regrouped. Table 1 explicitly displays sublinear alternatives; Figures 1–2 gain ProjGD curves and legends.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects v2's Algorithm 2 acceptance loop and excludes the singular rho = mu case in Lemma C.5, improving implementability and precision. Clearer explanations, reduced duplication and the ProjGD comparison provide further limited benefits. These gains are qualified by a new error: Example E.5(i) claims 6 log(1+x^2) ≥ x^2 throughout [f ≤ 16], which fails at x = 5. The central convergence results and existing empirical tables remain unchanged.
